original_question: Which type of antibody-producing white blood cells are found to densely infiltrate a syringocystadenoma papilliferum?

final_qi.question: Which type of antibody-producing white blood cells are found to densely infiltrate a syringocystadenoma papilliferum?
final_qi.search_keyword: antibody-producing white blood cells infiltrate syringocystadenoma papilliferum
final_qi.long_answer: Syringocystadenoma papilliferum is a benign sweat gland tumor that is often characterized histologically by a dense infiltrate of plasma cells. Plasma cells are antibody-producing white blood cells derived from B lymphocytes. These cells mature in response to antigen exposure and are responsible for secreting large amounts of antibodies, which can be seen in the inflammatory response associated with this lesion.
